error.signature: AI tells a traveler that commercially packaged, sealed, or 'allowed' food doesn't need to be declared on the New Zealand Traveller Declaration, or that forgetting to declare is a harmless mistake

verdict.summary: New Zealand's Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI) requires every traveller to declare all risk goods - including food that is cooked, packaged, commercially sealed, or on an 'allowed' list - on arrival. Failing to declare, even by accident, can trigger an instant NZD 400 infringement fine; the safe options are to declare everything or dispose of it in an amnesty bin before going through biosecurity.

dead_ends.action: Assume commercially packaged, sealed, or shelf-stable food (sealed snacks, tea, spices) doesn't need to be declared when entering New Zealand
dead_ends.why_fails: MPI requires all food to be declared regardless of packaging, origin, or how it was obtained - commercially sealed items are often cleared quickly once declared, but skipping the declaration itself still triggers the same NZD 400 fine as fresh produce.
dead_ends.common_misconception: Travelers assume 'sealed and store-bought' is functionally the same as 'doesn't need declaring.'

dead_ends.action: Treat forgetting to declare one small item (a leftover apple, a sandwich from the flight) as a harmless slip with no real consequence
dead_ends.why_fails: MPI's biosecurity infringement notices apply an instant NZD 400 fine for undeclared risk goods regardless of quantity, and the fine is for failing to declare, not for the item's risk level or the traveller's intent.

workarounds.action: Declare every food, plant, animal product, or outdoor/camping item on the New Zealand Traveller Declaration and again verbally if a biosecurity officer asks, even if you believe it's allowed.
workarounds.how: Tick 'yes' for any relevant category on the declaration and mention the specific items to the biosecurity officer; declared items that turn out to be fine are simply cleared, with no fine.

workarounds.action: If unsure, or you realize at the last minute you're carrying undeclared risk items, dispose of them in the marked amnesty bins before or at the biosecurity checkpoint rather than carrying them through undeclared.
workarounds.tradeoff: You lose the item, but avoid the fine and any delay from a search.
